_comment: The agent harness configuration. ONE file, two readers (config.ps1 for the
scripts, config.py for the Mattermost bridge), so a value is never defined
twice in two languages. Precedence, resolved only in the loaders:
built-in defaults < this file < harness.local.json (gitignored) < environment
This file is committed and MUST NOT contain secrets - it holds policy and
topology only. Machine-specific or experimental overrides go in

extension._why_locked: operator 2026-08-28: the surface the operator drives interactively must never silently degrade to a weaker model.

mattermost._note: switchable in a thread with 'profile: <name>', the same shape as the existing 'model:' and 'worktree:' directives.

_runners_comment: THE SHARED RUNNER REGISTRY (dark-factory-unification U4). A runner is an execution
SUBSTRATE - what runs a role, of what kind, at what address - which is the one object
this harness and agent-org genuinely have in common. agent-org held the same facts as a
bare CSV of URLs (AO_WORKER_INSTANCE_URLS, kind implicit); it now reads THIS block
(agent-org/agent-bridge/app/modules/runners.py), which is why the ao-worker pool is
declared here. Their PROFILE tables did NOT merge and should not: agent-org's profile
binds a role to a model LANE for the bridge's own inference calls, this one binds a role
pooled says whether an orchestrator may ACQUIRE the row's addresses as work capacity.
It is not a synonym for addressable: the coder plane's little-coder is addressable and
is NOT pooled, because it is the operator's interactive daemon on one shared workspace, and
sharing an executor between interactive and automated work is a collision little-coder's
reachable_from is load-bearing, not documentation: it names the vantage points that can
actually open the endpoint, and scripts/agent-harness/check-runner-endpoints.ps1 fails
when the declaration and reality disagree in EITHER direction. It exists because this
file claimed little-coder was at http://127.0.0.1:8090 for as long as nothing dispatched
- the coder plane publishes only 127.0.0.1:9091 (metrics), so that address was refused
by the host every single time. A runner nothing calls is a runner nothing corrects.

claude-code._note: a Claude Code agent - a subagent in an editor session, or 'claude -p' spawned by the bridge. Model names are CLI aliases, not API ids. It runs ON the host, in a worktree; it has no task endpoint, which is why agent-org cannot yet use one as a pooled worker (RunnerDispatch raises RunnerNotProvisioned for this kind).

little-coder._note: the coder plane's daemon. NOT pooled: it is the operator's interactive coder and its /workspace is a single shared volume, so an orchestrator acquiring it would collide with a human mid-task - little-coder's own design rejected sharing an executor between interactive and automated work as a deterministic collision (documentation/implementation-guide/little-coder/Self-improving-little-coder-design.md:656). NOT reachable from the host: coder/docker-compose.yml publishes 127.0.0.1:9091 (metrics) and nothing else, so a host-side dispatcher must either be given a published 8090 or run inside one of the networks above. Still unproven: no work item has completed through it - do not read config support as a proven feature.

agent-org-worker._note: agent-org's governed worker pool, declared here so both systems read one list - the 'agent-org workers as harness runners' half of U4. PROVEN in agent-org (it is the substrate its efforts have always run on), which is a different claim from proven as a HARNESS runner: a harness item lives in a host worktree and these daemons only ever work on a workspace they cloned themselves, so handing one an item means handing over a BRANCH, never a path. Reachability is the same story as little-coder above: container networks only.

all-cloud._desc: the default everywhere; all three roles on cloud opus

all-local._desc: no cloud calls at all; needs the inference plane healthy

local-work-cloud-review._desc: cheap production, expensive judgement - the reviewer is the last gate before a merge

cloud-work-local-test._desc: expensive production, cheap verification - useful when the test plan is mechanical

pipeline._note: the role -> state -> duty table stays in queue.ps1: it is behavior, not tuning. Turning a gate off here is an operator decision with a real cost, which is why both are listed explicitly rather than assumed.

_env_files_note: Runtime files a worktree needs but git will not materialize. The two recipe
.env files live INSIDE the OB1 submodule, so a fresh worktree clone never has
them and `docker compose -f OB1/docker/docker-compose.yml config` fails there
while passing in the main checkout - which is how the offline harness came to
fail only in worktrees. An ARRAY of lines, like _comment above: a JSON string
cannot contain a raw newline, and the first version of this note did. PowerShell
ConvertFrom-Json accepted it; Python json.loads did not - and this file has BOTH
readers (config.ps1 and config.py), so it would have broken the bridge alone.
